summary: Stand up the validation suite first: environment, cantilever against beam theory, NAFEMS LE10 timing at three densities, thermal slab, and a CalculiX vs scikit-fem cross-check. Tasks T1-T2 run in P0; T3-T4 run once the P1 pipeline exists.
reuse: docs/research/competitive-landscape-2026-11.md: LE10 reference −5.38 MPa, FeenoX timing as the only public reference point

tasks.task: Create environment.yml and a smoke test that runs cadquery, gmsh and ccx on the demo laptop.
steps: 1. Download the micromamba executable into the micromamba folder of the user profile.
2. Write environment.yml (name attome-ae, channel conda-forge): python=3.12, cadquery, build123d, gmsh, calculix, meshio, pyvista, optuna, pymoo, scikit-fem, numpy, scipy, pydantic, pytest.
3. Create the environment with micromamba create -y -f environment.yml.

4. Write tests/test_smoke.py: build a 10x10x10 mm CadQuery box, export STEP, mesh it with the gmsh executable, solve a one-element cube with ccx against the analytical elongation, and assert each step succeeds (ccx -v exits 201 by design).
5. Record the installed versions of ccx and gmsh in docs/environment.md.
verify: micromamba run -n attome-ae python -m pytest tests/test_smoke.py -q
tasks.done_when: The smoke test passes on the demo laptop from a fresh environment.
do_not: do not build CalculiX from source
do not pin versions that conda-forge does not provide for win-64
tasks.stop_and_ask_if: conda-forge has no working win-64 calculix build; then propose WSL2 with the exact commands.

tasks.task: Solve NAFEMS LE10 with ccx at three mesh densities and record error and runtime.
steps: 1. Build the LE10 thick elliptic plate geometry with CadQuery from the published NAFEMS dimensions.
2. Mesh with gmsh at three sizes (coarse, medium, fine) using second-order tetrahedra.
3. Write the CalculiX deck with the LE10 boundary conditions and 1 MPa pressure on the top face.
4. Run ccx, read sigma_yy at point D from the .dat output, compute the error against −5.38 MPa.
5. Time each run (wall clock) and record nodes, elements, DOF, sigma_yy, error % and seconds in docs/benchmarks.md.
verify: prints three rows; fine-mesh error under 2%
tasks.done_when: docs/benchmarks.md has a measured LE10 table for the demo laptop.
do_not: do not use linear tetrahedra for the stress result
do not quote FeenoX numbers as our numbers
tasks.stop_and_ask_if: the fine-mesh error is above 5% after checking the node-order mapping.

tasks.task: Add the cantilever and thermal slab cases and run the whole suite with pytest.
steps: 1. Cantilever: 100x10x10 mm steel beam, 100 N tip load, compare tip deflection with P*L^3/(3*E*I) through structura.solve.calculix.
2. Thermal slab: 1D conduction through a 10 mm plate with fixed temperatures, compare the mid-plane temperature with the linear solution.
3. Wrap LE10 as a pytest that asserts the medium-mesh error is under 3%.
4. Mark all three with @pytest.mark.validation.
verify: micromamba run -n attome-ae python -m pytest -m validation -q
tasks.done_when: The validation suite passes and runs in under five minutes.
do_not: do not loosen a tolerance to make a case pass
tasks.stop_and_ask_if: a case fails by more than its tolerance after one fix attempt.

tasks.task: Cross-check CalculiX against scikit-fem on the same bracket mesh.
steps: 1. Read the gmsh mesh with meshio and assemble linear elasticity with scikit-fem on quadratic tetrahedra.
2. Apply the same fixed faces and load as the CalculiX deck from the bracket template's physical groups.
3. Compare maximum displacement and the displacement at the load face centroid.
4. Assert both differ by less than 3%.
verify: micromamba run -n attome-ae python -m pytest tests/validation/test_crosscheck.py -q
tasks.done_when: CalculiX and scikit-fem agree within 3% on displacement for the bracket.
do_not: do not change the CalculiX deck to match scikit-fem
tasks.stop_and_ask_if: the two solvers disagree by more than 10%.

tasks.task: Add LE1, Euler buckling, modal and fin cases, golden results and the generated validation report.
tasks.where: new files tests/validation/test_le1.py, tests/validation/test_buckling_modal.py, tests/validation/test_fin.py, tests/validation/golden/, scripts/validation_report.py, docs/validation.md
steps: 1. NAFEMS LE1 elliptic membrane: assert sigma_yy at point D within 3% of 92.7 MPa on the medium mesh.
2. Euler column (pinned-pinned): buckling load factor within 3% of pi^2*E*I/L^2 divided by the applied load.
3. Cantilever modal: first natural frequency within 3% of the Euler-Bernoulli value.
4. Single straight fin with fixed base temperature and film coefficient: tip temperature within 3% of the analytical fin solution.
5. Store the demo designs' key results in tests/validation/golden/ and fail when any moves by more than 0.5%.
6. scripts/validation_report.py runs the suite and writes docs/validation.md with reference, our value, error, mesh size and runtime per case.
verify: micromamba run -n attome-ae python -m pytest -m validation -q && micromamba run -n attome-ae python scripts/validation_report.py
tasks.done_when: Every structural and thermal case passes and the public report is generated from the run.
do_not: do not edit docs/validation.md by hand
do not update golden results without a written reason in the commit message
tasks.stop_and_ask_if: a NAFEMS case misses its tolerance after checking units and node order.

acceptance: Smoke test, cantilever, thermal slab, LE10 and cross-check pass with pytest -m validation
docs/benchmarks.md holds measured LE10 runtimes for three densities
docs/validation.md generated from the suite with LE1, LE10, buckling, modal and thermal cases
risks: A wrong node-order mapping passes displacement checks but gives wrong stress; LE10 checks stress directly.
